official_questions.stem: Which of the following is not a federal feature of the Indian Constitution?
official_questions.core_fact: Federal features: written and rigid constitution, division of powers, supremacy of the Constitution, independent judiciary, bicameralism. The CAG audits both Union and State accounts under one integrated system - a unitary feature.

Distribution of powers is a federal feature of the Indian Constitution.
The Comptroller and Auditor General is a federal feature of the Indian Constitution.
statements.fact: The CAG (single integrated audit machinery for Union and States) is a unitary feature.

statements.t: An independent Supreme Court is a federal feature of the Indian Constitution.

official_questions.rule: Unitary list: single citizenship, single constitution, integrated judiciary, All-India Services, CAG, Governor appointed by Centre, emergency provisions.

official_questions.stem: Find out the wrong statement regarding the Punchhi Commission Recommendations
options: Punchhi Commission was constituted by the UPA government to study Centre State relations
The Commission recommended that Governor nominee should not have participated in active politics at least for a couple of years previous to his appointment
The Commission recommended that there is no need to amend Article 355 and 356
The Commission also criticised arbitrary dismissal of Governor
official_questions.key: The Commission recommended that there is no need to amend Article 355 and 356
official_questions.core_fact: The Punchhi Commission (set up April 2007 by the UPA govt; report 2010) recommended amending Arts 355 and 356 to allow 'localised emergency' (district/part of State, max 3 months), fixed 5-year tenure for Governors and removal only by a State Legislature resolution; Governor should not have been in active politics for a couple of years before appointment.

statements.t: The Punchhi Commission was constituted by the UPA government to study Centre-State relations.
The Commission recommended that a Governor nominee should not have participated in active politics for at least a couple of years before appointment.
The Commission recommended that there is no need to amend Articles 355 and 356.
statements.fact: Punchhi recommended amending Arts 355/356 to enable localised emergency for up to 3 months.

statements.t: The Commission also criticised the arbitrary dismissal of Governors.

official_questions.rule: Punchhi (2007-10): localised emergency, 5-yr Governor tenure, Governor removal by state legislature, cooling-off for politicians.

official_questions.stem: Which of the following is not one of the recommendation of the Rajmannar Committee.

statements.t: The Rajamannar Committee recommended the creation of an Inter-State Council.
The Rajamannar Committee recommended curbing the misuse of Article 356.
The Rajamannar Committee recommended the abolition of the IAS and IPS.
The Rajamannar Committee recommended strengthening the Governor system.
statements.fact: Rajamannar wanted the Governor's powers curbed and State autonomy increased.

official_questions.rule: Rajamannar (TN 1969): pro-State autonomy; Sarkaria (Centre 1983) and Punchhi (Centre 2007) are central commissions.

official_questions.stem:
Which of the following violate the federal principles of the Indian Constitution ?
A. Office of the Governor
B. Central Services
C. Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General
D. Emergency Powers
official_questions.core_fact: Departures from federal principles: Governor appointed by and holding office at the pleasure of the President; a single CAG auditing Union and State accounts; emergency powers converting the federation into a unitary State. Central Services (Union-only cadres) do not touch State autonomy; the All-India Services (Art. 312) do.

statements.t: The office of the Governor violates the federal principles of the Indian Constitution.
The Central Services violate the federal principles of the Indian Constitution.
statements.fact: Central Services work only on Union subjects; the All-India Services are the feature criticised as anti-federal.

statements.t: The office of the Comptroller and Auditor General violates the federal principles of the Indian Constitution.
Emergency powers violate the federal principles of the Indian Constitution.

official_questions.rule: Central Services (Union only) vs All-India Services (IAS/IPS/IFoS, Art. 312, serve States, controlled by Centre).

official_questions.stem:

Reason (R) : The All India Service officers are governed by Central Government rules and the State Governments do not have full control over them.

official_questions.core_fact: All-India Services (Art. 312) serve both Union and States but are recruited by UPSC and governed by central rules (AIS Act 1951); States cannot dismiss or fully discipline them - hence criticised as violating federalism and State autonomy.

statements.t: The All-India Services violate the federal principle of the Constitution as well as the autonomy of States.
All-India Service officers are governed by Central Government rules and the State Governments do not have full control over them.
R explains A: central control over AIS officers is why AIS are said to violate federal principles.

official_questions.rule: AIS: created by Parliament after RS resolution (Art. 312); Centre recruits, trains, disciplines; States only post.

official_questions.stem:
Which of the following will be the correct consequences of declaration of National Emergency by the President ?
A. The President can modify the constitutional distribution of finances between the Center and the States.
B. The Center becomes entitled to give executive directions to a State on any matter.
C. The President can suspend all the Fundamental Rights of the citizens.
official_questions.core_fact: During a National Emergency: the Centre may give executive directions to any State on any matter (Art. 353(a)); Parliament may legislate on State List (Art. 250); the President may modify distribution of revenues (Art. 354); Art. 19 is suspended (Art. 358, war/external aggression only) and the President may suspend enforcement of other FRs except Arts 20 and 21 (Art. 359, 44th Amendment 1978).

statements.t: During a National Emergency the President can modify the constitutional distribution of finances between the Centre and the States.
During a National Emergency the Centre becomes entitled to give executive directions to a State on any matter.
During a National Emergency the President can suspend all the Fundamental Rights of the citizens.
statements.fact: The President may suspend enforcement of FRs except Arts 20 and 21 (44th Amendment).

official_questions.rule: Art. 358 suspends Art. 19 automatically (war/external aggression); Art. 359 suspends enforcement of others except 20 and 21.

official_questions.stem: Which of the following is not a condition for the political party to be recognised as National Party ?

The party, at a general election to Lok Sabha or Legislative Assembly, polls six percent of valid votes in any four or more States and in addition it wins four Lok Sabha seats from any State or States
It is recognised as a State party in any four States
official_questions.core_fact: Election Symbols Order 1968 para 6B: a party is national if (a) it polls 6% of valid votes in 4+ States in LS/Assembly elections and wins 4 LS seats; or (b) wins 2% of LS seats (11) from at least 3 States; or (c) is recognised as a State party in 4 States. All three listed are conditions.

statements.t: The party wins two percent of seats in the Lok Sabha from at least three different states - this is one of the conditions for recognition as a National Party.
statements.d: The party wins two percent of seats in the Lok Sabha from at least three different states

statements.d: The party polls six percent of valid votes in any four or more States and in addition wins four Lok Sabha seats

statements.t: It is recognised as a State party in any four States - this is one of the conditions for recognition as a National Party.
statements.d: It is recognised as a State party in any four States

statements.t: None of the above (every listed item is a condition) - this is one of the conditions for recognition as a National Party.
statements.d: None of the above (every listed item is a condition)

official_questions.rule: National party: 6% in 4 States + 4 LS seats / 2% LS seats from 3 States / State party in 4 States.

official_questions.stem:
Consider the following statements :
Assertion (A) : One of the most controversial Articles in the Constitution is Article 356.
Reason (R) : It is imposed when the Government of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
official_questions.key: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 356 (President's Rule) applies when the President is satisfied that the State government cannot be carried on per the Constitution; its broad subjective ground led to frequent misuse (over 100 times) and controversy, checked by S.R. Bommai (1994).

statements.t: One of the most controversial Articles in the Constitution is Article 356.
It is imposed when the Government of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.
statements.d: cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions

statements.t: R explains A: its broad ground (failure of constitutional machinery) is why Art. 356 is controversial.

official_questions.rule: Art. 356: 'dead letter' hope (Ambedkar) vs misuse; Bommai 1994 made it judicially reviewable; floor test.

official_questions.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct ?
i. Under Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act (RPA) 1951, no election can be called in question except by an election petition presented in accordance with the provisions of this part.
ii. Only the High Courts have original jurisdiction on deciding on election petitions.
iii. An election petition calling in question an election shall be filed within the time period of 30 days from the date of declaration of results.
official_questions.core_fact: RPA 1951: S.80 – no election can be questioned except by an election petition; S.80A – the High Court tries election petitions; S.81 – petition to be presented within 45 days of the date of election of the returned candidate.

statements.t: Under Section 81 of the RPA 1951, no election can be called in question except by an election petition presented in accordance with the provisions of this part.
statements.fact: The bar is in Section 80; Section 81 deals with presentation of petitions.

statements.t: Only the High Courts have original jurisdiction on deciding on election petitions.
An election petition calling in question an election shall be filed within 30 days from the date of declaration of results.
statements.fact: The limitation period is 45 days.

official_questions.rule: RPA Part VI: 80 = bar, 80A = High Court, 81 = 45-day presentation; Art 71 sends President/VP disputes to SC.
official_questions.key_note: 'Only the High Courts' is true for RPA elections; Presidential/VP election disputes are decided by the Supreme Court (Art 71).

official_questions.stem:
Which of the following statements is/are not true regarding Electronic Voting Machines (EVM) ?
A. EVMs were used for the first time in the entire State of Goa in the general elections to the Assembly in 1999.
B. EVMs were used for the first time on experimental basis in the selected constituencies in the Assembly elections to the States of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat in 1998.
options: Both A and B are true
official_questions.core_fact: EVMs were first used in 1982 at Paravur (Kerala); on an experimental basis they were used in 16 Assembly constituencies of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi (NCT) in Nov 1998; Goa (1999) was the first State to use EVMs in all constituencies.

statements.t: EVMs were used for the first time in the entire State of Goa in the general elections to the Assembly in 1999.
EVMs were used for the first time on an experimental basis in selected constituencies in the Assembly elections of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat in 1998.
statements.fact: The 1998 trial covered 16 constituencies in Rajasthan, MP and Delhi; first ever use was Paravur (Kerala) 1982.

official_questions.rule: EVM timeline: Paravur 1982, Rajasthan/MP/Delhi 1998, Goa 1999 full State, all LS seats 2004, VVPAT 2013 (Noksen, Nagaland).
